page-widgets.statement: The Financial Risk page shows the organization's risk score-based financial exposure and the exposure without Zscaler, an estimate of the reduction from implementing the Top 10 Financial Contributing Factors' recommended actions, and the loss estimate change over the last 6 months.

quotes: View our organization's risk score-based financial exposure and the exposure without Zscaler.
The section also provides an estimate of how much of this financial risk exposure can be reduced by implementing the recommended actions from the Top 10 Financial Contributing Factors section.
The graph shows the loss estimate change over the last 6 months.
potential financial loss exposure for your current risk score
view the loss curve over time to take appropriate actions

top-factors.statement: The Top 10 Financial Contributing Factors table gives each factor's Financial Exposure as a loss estimate in US dollars, plus a Licensed? value.

quotes: View the top 10 factors contributing to your organization's financial risk exposure.
Financial Exposure: The financial loss estimate is in US dollars.
Licensed?: Whether you are subscribed to the required feature to implement the recommended action (Y for Yes and N for No).

factors-csv.statement: The Financial Risk page can download the complete list of factors affecting the financial risk to a CSV file.

quotes: Download the complete list of factors affecting the financial risk to a CSV file.

settings-values.statement: Financial Risk Settings show default values set during onboarding, which can be customized by industry vertical and industry annual revenue range; Reset to Default restores the defaults.

quotes: Under the Default Values, you can view the default values set for your organization during onboarding.
Industry Vertical: Select the industry vertical that best represents your organization.
Industry Annual Revenue Range: Select the annual revenue range for the organization's industry vertical.
You can click Reset to Default if you want the Risk360 service to use the default values for calculation.

settings-loss-range.statement: The Financial Loss Range is the lower and upper bounds of the financial loss if the organization faces a breach, and these values are used for simulating financial loss estimations within the range.

quotes: Financial Loss Range: Enter the lower and upper bounds of the financial loss, in case your organization faces a breach. These values are used for simulating financial loss estimations within the set range.

settings-inherit.statement: The Financial Risk model inherits the latest values from the preceding settings to perform loss estimations.

quotes: The Financial Risk model inherits the latest values from the preceding settings to perform loss estimations.

mc-page-metrics.statement: The Monte Carlo Simulation page shows a Loss Exceedance graph of the probability of exceeding loss values in millions of dollars, an Average Yearly Exposure bar graph of average yearly loss in millions of dollars per risk parameter, and Breach Probability (%) calculated from inherent, last 30 days average, residual and industry peer risk.

quotes: This graph shows the probability of exceeding loss values (in percentage) in millions of dollars.
This bar graph shows the average yearly loss in millions of dollars for each of the risk parameters.
This section shows the breach probability percentage calculated based on your organization's inherent risks, last 30 days average risk, residual risk, and industry peer risk.

mc-breach-probability.statement: The Zscaler-computed breach probability is continuously updated, is determined from industry vertical, annual revenue range and risk score, and is an input to the financial exposure calculation.

quotes: The breach probability is also an input parameter for your organization's financial exposure calculation.
The value of Zscaler-computed breach probability is continuously updated and determined based on the industry vertical, annual revenue range, and the organization's risk score.

mc-simulate-toggle.statement: Enabling the Simulate toggle lets the breach probability be edited per risk parameter; after Apply the financial exposure is reevaluated, and disabling the toggle restores the Zscaler-computed probabilities.

quotes: You can enable the Simulate toggle to edit the probability for the desired risk parameter. After you click Apply, your organization's financial exposure is reevaluated based on your input. Disable the toggle to restore the Zscaler-computed probabilities.

mc-iterations.statement: The Simulation Results drawer has 4 tabs, one per risk parameter, each showing all 1,000 iterations; the page states the service runs the Monte Carlo simulations 1,000 times.

quotes: The Risk360 service runs the Monte Carlo simulations 1,000 times.
The drawer consists of 4 tabs for each risk parameter. Each tab shows the results for all the 1,000 iterations run by the Monte Carlo Simulation.

model-method.title: The financial model's loss-curve formula, exposure-without-Zscaler method and confidence level
model-method.detail: The Financial Risk, settings and Monte Carlo Simulation pages do not publish the loss-curve formula, how the exposure without Zscaler is estimated, or a confidence level for the interval, and they do not state a per-day cadence for the simulation. The Monte Carlo explainer defines the interval by a loss's lower and upper bounds, which the Financial Loss Range setting exposes (risk360.scoring:monte-carlo-runs, settings-loss-range).
